domain_label: Study System — Multimodal Capture & Voice Answering (spoken answers, any language, batch STT, privacy)
purpose: A method for capturing a learner's spoken answers and voice notes in any language and turning them into graded, learner-model-updating text through an asynchronous batch speech-to-text pipeline whose local-whisper-class vs cloud-STT engine is a deferred per-owner config choice behind one interface, while holding the privacy constraints that voice is personal (and speaker-ID-grade biometric) data — choosing the capture and queue model, sizing the local Whisper-class engine against hardware, cataloguing the cloud STT options and their language coverage honestly (naming the counts that are UNKNOWN), grading answer CONTENT from the transcript rather than pronunciation, and never running speaker identification — without inventing a language count, retention term, or accuracy figure the research did not verify.
assumptions: no live benchmark of transcription accuracy or grading quality on this learner's own audio is supplied; language-coverage counts, memory footprints and retention terms are quoted only where the research file verified them (fetched or via search snippet) and are otherwise held UNKNOWN, never invented
the owner explicitly deferred the local-vs-cloud STT decision, so the architecture must keep both paths open behind one interface and treat the engine as a config flag, not a rewrite
the system is single-user, so there is no product need to identify the speaker; the recordings are always the one known learner's own voice
the owner's 'saved and queued for later analysis' implies an asynchronous nightly batch pipeline with no real-time latency constraint, aligned with the system's every-night analysis mode
Whisper's own per-language accuracy varies strongly (the repo publishes WER breakdowns), so 'any language' means coverage exists, not that every language transcribes equally well
exclusions: the gamification / visual-progress calendar, streak and habit-psychology material (Part A of the research file) belongs to the engagement/UX specialist and is not covered here

the flashcard-quality and book-decomposition rules that the voice-note LLM post-processor feeds into live in the flashcards specialist; this KB stops at producing note/flashcard CANDIDATES for human confirmation
the learner-model / scheduler internals that consume the grading write-back (mastery update maths, SRS interval logic) belong to the scheduler specialist; this KB stops at the write-back contract
stating a fabricated cloud STT language count (Azure and Amazon current counts are UNKNOWN), a fabricated per-language accuracy number, or a fabricated non-OpenAI vendor retention term as fact

real-time / streaming ASR, wake-word or always-listening capture, and on-device delivery/pronunciation scoring engines beyond naming that the audio path must stay open for a future delivery-scoring step

competency_questions.question: Why is the local-vs-cloud STT engine a deferred config choice behind one interface rather than a hard-coded pick, and what architectural seam does that force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWNER_DEFERRED_CHOICE states the owner deferred the local-vs-cloud decision and TRANSCRIBER_INTERFACE names the single interface with LocalWhisper and CloudSTT implementations so the decision is a config flag, not a rewrite

competency_questions.question: Why is the capture pipeline asynchronous batch rather than real-time, and how does audio get captured and enqueued?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASYNC_QUEUE_POSTURE derives the async batch pipeline from the owner's 'saved and queued' wording, AUDIO_CAPTURE_SPEC states one 16 kHz mono file per answer, and STORE_ENQUEUE_MODEL gives the metadata row with status=queued and the dir-of-files + SQLite store

competency_questions.question: What is the local Whisper-class STT option, how many languages does it cover, and what hardware does it need?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_WHISPER_FAMILY states Whisper's tokenizer LANGUAGES dict has 100 entries (fetched, machine-counted) and WHISPER_CPP_FOOTPRINT gives the per-model memory table (large ~2.9 GiB disk / ~3.9 GB RAM, runs under 4 GB on CPU)

competency_questions.question: When is faster-whisper the right local path and how is the local model size chosen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FASTER_WHISPER_PATH states the CTranslate2 up-to-4x-faster claim and its CUDA-12/cuDNN-9 GPU requirement, and LOCAL_MODEL_SIZING concludes that overnight batch has no latency constraint so CPU whisper.cpp medium/large suffices and faster-whisper is used only if an NVIDIA GPU is present

competency_questions.question: What cloud STT options exist, what language support do they claim, and which counts are UNKNOWN?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLOUD_STT_LANDSCAPE lists Google (125+ vendor claim), Azure (large table, exact count UNKNOWN), Amazon Transcribe (31 as of a blog date, current count UNKNOWN), OpenAI Audio API (whisper-1 25 MB limit + gpt-4o-transcribe family, ~57 listed languages) and names Deepgram/AssemblyAI as existing without inventing their numbers

competency_questions.question: How does the system handle 'whatever language' without asking the user to declare it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LANGUAGE_ID_HANDLING states Whisper's built-in language identification detects the language, that the detected language plus confidence is stored, and that per-language accuracy varies (repo WER breakdowns) so coverage is not equal quality

competency_questions.question: How is the nightly transcription worker structured and what happens when an item fails?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATCH_TRANSCRIBE_WORKER drains status=queued through the TranscriberInterface nightly, and FAILURE_HANDLING_STATES gives the queued -> transcribed -> graded | failed(reason) state machine with retry-next-night and nothing-silently-dropped

competency_questions.question: How is a spoken answer graded, and why grade the transcript content rather than the pronunciation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LLM_GRADE_RUBRIC feeds transcript + question rubric to an LLM grader producing score/subscores/misconception tags, and DELIVERY_VS_CONTENT_SCORING grades content from the transcript and keeps the audio for a future delivery-scoring step reserved for TOEFL-speaking-style delivery

competency_questions.question: Is automated grading of spoken answers established practice, and what precedent supports it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPEECHRATER_PRECEDENT states ETS has operated SpeechRater on TOEFL spontaneous speech since ~2008 in a human+machine combination, and notes the exact current human/machine weighting is UNKNOWN

competency_questions.question: How does grading output reach the rest of the study system, and what audit trail is kept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEARNER_MODEL_WRITEBACK updates the per-item mastery state and weakness map for the scheduler and keeps audio + transcript + grade linked so a learner can ask why an answer was marked wrong

competency_questions.question: How is voice note-making different from answer grading, and where is the human kept in the loop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOICE_NOTE_PIPELINE reuses record -> transcribe minus grading, adds LLM cleanup/structuring into note/flashcard candidates, uses Whisper word timestamps to link a note to its audio moment, and requires human confirmation before anything enters the KB

competency_questions.question: What are the privacy constraints on voice data, why is speaker-ID never run, and what changes if cloud STT is chosen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOICE_PRIVACY_CONSTRAINT states voice is personal data and becomes Article 9 special-category biometric data when processed to identify a person, so speaker-ID is never run, and CLOUD_RETENTION_CONSENT states OpenAI's not-trained-by-default + up-to-30-day abuse retention, flags other vendors' terms as UNKNOWN, and requires a consent note + the chosen vendor's retention terms before enabling cloud

competency_questions.question: What is the merged go/no-go for shipping the voice-capture pipeline?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAPTURE_GO_NOGO composes the verdict: the async queue and interface are in place, a default (local) engine is sized to hardware, language ID handles any language, grading writes back with an audit link, failures never drop, and the privacy posture (no speaker-ID; cloud only behind consent + retention terms) holds

glossary.definition: The owner explicitly postponed the decision between local (whisper-class) and cloud STT ('the local AI or the cloud, later on decision'), so the architecture keeps both paths open behind one interface and the engine becomes a config flag rather than a code rewrite.

The record -> store+enqueue -> nightly transcribe -> grade -> write-back flow implied by the owner's 'saved and queued for later analysis'; because nothing is real-time, no low-latency ASR is needed and a directory of audio files plus a SQLite status table is sufficient at single-user scale.

OpenAI Whisper's tokenizer LANGUAGES dict contains exactly 100 entries (machine-counted from the fetched tokenizer.py); the commonly cited ~99 figure predates Cantonese (yue) being added with large-v3. This is the coverage ceiling for the local path, but per-language accuracy (WER) varies strongly.

The dependency-free C/C++ Whisper build that runs CPU-first across desktop, phone and Raspberry Pi; fetched memory table: tiny 75 MiB/~273 MB RAM, base 142 MiB/~388 MB, small 466 MiB/~852 MB, medium 1.5 GiB/~2.1 GB, large 2.9 GiB/~3.9 GB, so the full multilingual model fits under 4 GB RAM on a normal laptop.

A reimplementation of Whisper on the CTranslate2 engine claiming up to 4x the speed of openai/whisper at equal accuracy with less memory; the GPU path needs CUDA 12 + cuDNN 9, and CPU-only is also supported.

Whisper's built-in ability to detect the spoken language rather than requiring the user to declare it; the system stores the detected language with its confidence, satisfying the owner's 'in whatever language' requirement without a language picker.

The single adapter seam with two implementations, LocalWhisper (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) and CloudSTT; the nightly worker drains the queue through it, so honouring the owner's deferred local-vs-cloud choice is a configuration change, not a rewrite.

The rule that the LLM grades the meaning/content recovered from the transcript, not pronunciation or fluency; delivery features live in the audio and are only scored for a TOEFL-speaking-style course, which is why the audio path is kept linked for a future delivery-scoring step.

ETS's automated engine for scoring spontaneous non-native speech, operated on TOEFL since ~2008; operational TOEFL iBT Speaking combines human raters (holistic content) with SpeechRater (analytic delivery), establishing that machine-grading transcribed speech is not exotic. Exact current human/machine weighting is UNKNOWN from the research.

Per the EDPB's Guidelines 02/2021 on Virtual Voice Assistants, voice recordings are personal data and become Article 9 special-category biometric data when processed to uniquely identify a person (speaker-ID, voice embeddings, identity diarization); plain transcription without an identification purpose does not by itself trigger Article 9, so the system never runs speaker identification.

nodes.definition: Establish the binding owner constraint that reshapes the architecture: the user should not always have to type, so ~10 questions can be answered by speaking in whatever language, and the answers are saved and queued for later AI analysis by 'the local AI or the cloud, later on decision' [FACT - owner's verbatim brief]. The local-vs-cloud STT engine choice is therefore explicitly deferred by the owner, and the architecture must keep both paths open behind one interface so the eventual pick is a config flag, not a rewrite. Voice note-making is also named as a first-class use of the same capture path.

included: the owner's speak-any-language, save-and-queue requirement
the explicit deferral of the local-vs-cloud engine decision
the keep-both-paths-open-behind-one-interface consequence
excluded: the concrete interface design (its own node)

pros.claim: Treating the engine as deferred prevents hard-coding a choice the owner has not made and having to unwind it later
pros.example: shipping the capture and queue now with local as the default while a cloud adapter waits behind the same interface

cons.claim: Keeping both paths open adds an abstraction that is wasted effort if the owner never switches engines
cons.example: maintaining a CloudSTT adapter that is never enabled because local coverage proved sufficient

failure_modes: hard-coding a single STT engine and forcing a rewrite when the owner decides the other way
reading 'later decision' as 'no decision needed' and skipping the abstraction seam entirely
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the owner's speak-any-language save-and-queue brief, marks the local-vs-cloud engine as owner-deferred, and derives the one-interface / config-flag consequence
revisit_triggers: the owner makes the local-vs-cloud decision
a new capture mode (e.g. video) is added to the brief
a cost or privacy event forces the engine choice early

base.update_signal: the owner resolves the local-vs-cloud decision or adds a capture mode

nodes.definition: Establish the 'whatever language' requirement as a first-class constraint: the learner may answer aloud in any language and must not be forced to declare which one. This pushes toward an STT engine with broad multilingual coverage AND built-in language identification, so the language is detected rather than asked for. 'Any language' means coverage must exist for the learner's languages, not that every language transcribes with equal accuracy — Whisper publishes per-language WER breakdowns showing wide variation, so the requirement is coverage-first with accuracy caveated per language.

included: the answer-in-any-language, no-language-picker requirement
the coverage-first vs equal-accuracy distinction
the pull toward a multilingual + language-ID engine
excluded: the specific engine's language count (its own node)

pros.claim: Requiring no language declaration removes friction from spoken capture and matches how a learner naturally speaks
pros.example: a learner answering one question in English and the next in Hindi without touching a language setting

cons.claim: Broad coverage hides that a rarer language may transcribe poorly, so 'supported' can mislead if accuracy is not caveated
cons.example: assuming a low-resource language transcribes as well as English because it is in the language list

failure_modes: forcing a language picker and breaking the natural spoken-answer flow
treating language coverage as uniform accuracy and mis-grading a poorly transcribed low-resource answer
acceptance_tests: the requirement states answer-in-any-language with no user declaration and separates coverage from per-language accuracy
revisit_triggers: a learner's primary language transcribes poorly
a new engine with wider or better low-resource coverage appears
the owner narrows the target languages

base.update_signal: a target-language accuracy result or a wider-coverage engine changes the requirement

nodes.definition: Derive the pipeline shape from the owner's 'saved and queued for later analysis': an asynchronous batch pipeline, not real-time ASR [ESTIMATE: design, HIGH]. Because nothing is transcribed live, there is no low-latency constraint, which is the cheap and robust choice — a directory of audio files plus a SQLite status table is fully sufficient at single-user scale and a message broker is overkill. The nightly transcription aligns with the study system's every-night analysis mode. This posture is the frame every downstream capture, transcription and grading node is built inside.

included: the async-batch (not real-time) derivation
the no-latency-constraint and files+SQLite-is-enough consequence
the nightly-batch alignment with the analysis mode
excluded: the worker and failure-state machine (their own nodes)

pros.claim: An async batch pipeline is the cheapest, most robust choice because it removes the real-time ASR constraint entirely
pros.example: draining the day's recorded answers overnight instead of transcribing each one live under a latency budget

cons.claim: Batch means a learner does not see their grade immediately, which can slow the feedback loop they feel
cons.example: an answer spoken in the morning not being graded until the nightly run

failure_modes: over-engineering a message broker and streaming ASR for a single-user overnight workload
coupling capture to live transcription so a slow engine blocks the learner mid-session
acceptance_tests: the analysis derives an async batch pipeline from 'saved and queued', states there is no real-time constraint, and prescribes a files + SQLite store aligned to the nightly run
revisit_triggers: a requirement for immediate in-session feedback appears
the audio volume outgrows a single-node SQLite store
the analysis mode moves off a nightly cadence

base.update_signal: an in-session-feedback need or an audio-volume scale change alters the posture

nodes.definition: Specify the capture itself: one audio file per spoken answer (and per voice note), stored lossless-enough compressed at 16 kHz mono — which is exactly what Whisper consumes, so no resampling loss is introduced downstream [ESTIMATE — design, research §B4; 16 kHz mono per Whisper's consumption noted there at ESTIMATE grade]. Capturing per-question rather than one long recording keeps each answer independently transcribable, gradable and retryable. The capture step is deliberately dumb: it records and hands off, doing no transcription, so a slow or unavailable engine never blocks the learner.

included: one 16 kHz mono file per answer/note
the per-question (not one-long-file) granularity
the record-and-hand-off, no-transcription-at-capture rule
excluded: the metadata row and queue status (its own node)

pros.claim: Recording 16 kHz mono per answer matches Whisper's input and keeps each answer independently processable
pros.example: re-transcribing a single failed answer without touching the rest of the session

cons.claim: Per-question files multiply small objects to track versus one session recording
cons.example: ten tiny files plus ten metadata rows for a ten-question session

failure_modes: capturing one long recording so a single answer cannot be retried in isolation
recording at a rate/format that forces a lossy resample before Whisper
acceptance_tests: the spec states one 16 kHz mono file per answer/note, per-question granularity, and that capture does no transcription
revisit_triggers: a future delivery-scoring step needs a higher sample rate
a capture-format mismatch forces resampling
voice notes need a different segmentation than answers

base.update_signal: a delivery-scoring sample-rate need or a format mismatch changes the capture spec

nodes.definition: Define the store-and-enqueue step: alongside each audio file write a metadata row {answer_id, question_id, session_id, recorded_at, duration, language_hint?, status: queued} [ESTIMATE: design]. A directory of audio files plus a SQLite table is the whole datastore at single-user scale; the status column is the queue. language_hint is optional because language identification handles undeclared language downstream. This is the durable handoff between the dumb capture step and the nightly worker: once a row is status=queued, the answer is safely parked for analysis and nothing is lost if the app closes.

included: the metadata row fields and status=queued
the dir-of-files + SQLite datastore = the queue
the optional language_hint deferring to LID
excluded: the worker that drains the queue (its own node)
the failure state transitions (its own node)

pros.claim: A SQLite status column IS the queue, giving durable, inspectable enqueue with no broker
pros.example: restarting the app and the nightly worker still finding every status=queued row intact

cons.claim: A single SQLite table caps concurrency and scale if the system ever grows past one user
cons.example: many concurrent writers contending on one SQLite file in a hypothetical multi-user future

failure_modes: writing the audio file without a durable metadata row so an answer is orphaned
baking a required language field and defeating the language-ID design
acceptance_tests: the model enumerates the metadata row with status=queued and states the files + SQLite store is the queue with language_hint optional
revisit_triggers: the system moves beyond single-user and SQLite concurrency binds
a new metadata field (e.g. device, consent flag) is needed
the queue needs cross-machine durability

base.update_signal: a multi-user move or a new metadata field changes the store model

nodes.definition: Define the architectural seam that honours the deferred choice: a single TranscriberInterface with two implementations — LocalWhisper (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) and CloudSTT — so the local-vs-cloud decision becomes a config flag, not a rewrite [ESTIMATE: design, HIGH]. The nightly worker calls only the interface; each implementation takes an audio file and returns {text, detected_language, confidence, word_timestamps?}. This is the node that operationalizes OWNER_DEFERRED_CHOICE: it is why the owner can decide local or cloud later without touching capture, queue, grading or write-back.

included: the one interface with LocalWhisper and CloudSTT implementations
the uniform {text, detected_language, confidence, word_timestamps?} return
the config-flag-not-rewrite property
excluded: the concrete local engine sizing and cloud catalogue (their own nodes)

pros.claim: One interface with two adapters makes the deferred engine choice a config change, isolating every other stage from it
pros.example: switching from LocalWhisper to CloudSTT by flipping a config value with grading and write-back untouched

cons.claim: A uniform return shape must cover both engines' capabilities, so an engine-specific feature (e.g. diarization) is flattened out
cons.example: a cloud feature that has no local equivalent being dropped to keep the interface uniform

failure_modes: leaking engine-specific calls into the worker so the config flag no longer suffices
designing a return shape that cannot carry word timestamps the voice-note pipeline needs
acceptance_tests: the interface names LocalWhisper and CloudSTT implementations, a uniform return including detected_language and optional word_timestamps, and the config-flag-not-rewrite guarantee
revisit_triggers: a new STT engine or capability must fit the interface
the return shape misses a field a downstream stage needs
the owner switches the configured engine

base.update_signal: a new engine, a missing return field, or an engine switch changes the interface

nodes.definition: Characterize the local Whisper-class engine's coverage: OpenAI Whisper's tokenizer LANGUAGES dict contains exactly 100 entries [FACT - fetched and machine-counted from whisper/tokenizer.py], covering en/zh/de/es/ru through yue (Cantonese, added with large-v3); the commonly cited '~99 languages' predates yue. Multilingual recognition, speech translation and language identification are core features [FACT - fetched openai/whisper]. Accuracy varies strongly by language and the repo publishes per-language WER breakdowns for large-v2/v3 [FACT - fetched]. For the owner's 'any language' requirement this 100-language set is the coverage ceiling of the local path.

included: the 100-entry LANGUAGES count as the local coverage ceiling
multilingual + translation + LID as core features
the per-language WER-varies caveat
excluded: the runtime memory footprint (its own node)

pros.claim: A machine-counted 100-language local model gives verifiable broad coverage with no per-transcription cost or data egress
pros.example: transcribing answers in any of 100 languages fully offline on the learner's own machine

cons.claim: Coverage is not uniform accuracy, so a low-resource language in the list may still transcribe poorly
cons.example: a language with high published WER producing a transcript too noisy to grade reliably

failure_modes: quoting '~99 languages' as if final when the fetched count is 100 including yue
treating every listed language as equally accurate and ignoring the WER breakdowns
acceptance_tests: the node states the fetched, machine-counted 100-language LANGUAGES count, names multilingual/translation/LID as core, and carries the per-language WER-varies caveat
revisit_triggers: a new Whisper release changes the language count or WER
a target language shows unacceptable WER
a non-Whisper local engine with better coverage appears

base.update_signal: a Whisper release or a target-language WER result changes the coverage picture

nodes.definition: Size the CPU-first local build: whisper.cpp is a dependency-free C/C++ implementation that runs on macOS, iOS, Android, Linux, FreeBSD, Windows, Raspberry Pi, WebAssembly and Docker, with acceleration via ARM NEON/Metal/Core ML, x86 AVX, CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan and OpenVINO, plus integer quantization, VAD and word-level timestamps [FACT - fetched ggml-org/whisper.cpp]. Fetched memory/disk table: tiny 75 MiB/~273 MB RAM, base 142 MiB/~388 MB, small 466 MiB/~852 MB, medium 1.5 GiB/~2.1 GB, large 2.9 GiB/~3.9 GB. So the full-quality multilingual model runs in under 4 GB RAM on CPU — feasible on a normal laptop, and the smaller models fit a phone [ESTIMATE - direct inference from the table, HIGH].

included: the platform/acceleration coverage and word-timestamp/VAD features
the fetched per-model memory/disk table
the runs-under-4GB-on-CPU and phone-fits-smaller inference
excluded: the faster-whisper GPU speed path (its own node)
the model-size selection decision (its own node)

pros.claim: A dependency-free CPU build that runs the large model under 4 GB RAM makes fully local transcription feasible on ordinary hardware
pros.example: running whisper.cpp large on a normal laptop overnight with no GPU and no cloud

cons.claim: CPU transcription is slower than GPU, so a large batch on a weak machine can run long
cons.example: a big backlog of answers taking many hours on a low-end CPU

failure_modes: assuming the large model needs more than 4 GB and reaching for cloud unnecessarily
picking a phone-sized model on a laptop and sacrificing accuracy for RAM headroom that exists
acceptance_tests: the node cites the fetched memory/disk table, states large runs under 4 GB RAM on CPU, and lists the platform/word-timestamp/VAD features
revisit_triggers: a new whisper.cpp release changes the footprint table
the target device's RAM is tighter than the chosen model
word timestamps or VAD behaviour changes

base.update_signal: a whisper.cpp release or a device-RAM constraint changes the footprint fit

nodes.definition: Characterize the fastest common local path: faster-whisper reimplements Whisper on the CTranslate2 inference engine and claims up to 4x faster than openai/whisper at the same accuracy with less memory (README benchmark: 13 min of audio in 1m03s fp16 vs 2m23s for openai/whisper on GPU) [FACT - fetched SYSTRAN/faster-whisper]. The GPU path requires CUDA 12 + cuDNN 9 (cuBLAS); CPU-only is also supported. This is the path to prefer when an NVIDIA GPU is present, trading a heavier dependency stack for throughput; without a GPU, whisper.cpp remains the simpler CPU-first choice.

included: the CTranslate2 up-to-4x-faster-same-accuracy claim and benchmark
the CUDA-12 / cuDNN-9 GPU requirement and CPU-only support
when-to-prefer-it (NVIDIA GPU present)
excluded: the final model-size decision (its own node)

pros.claim: Up to 4x throughput at equal accuracy clears a large overnight backlog fast when a GPU is available
pros.example: transcribing a heavy day's answers in a fraction of the time on an NVIDIA GPU

cons.claim: The GPU path pulls in a CUDA 12 + cuDNN 9 dependency stack that a plain laptop may not have
cons.example: a machine without an NVIDIA GPU gaining nothing from faster-whisper's GPU claim

failure_modes: reaching for faster-whisper's GPU speed on a machine with no NVIDIA GPU
adding the CUDA/cuDNN stack when the overnight batch has no latency pressure to justify it
acceptance_tests: the node states the CTranslate2 up-to-4x claim with its benchmark, the CUDA-12/cuDNN-9 requirement, and that it is preferred only when an NVIDIA GPU is present
revisit_triggers: an NVIDIA GPU becomes available or is removed
a faster-whisper release changes the speed/accuracy trade
the batch grows enough that CPU time binds

base.update_signal: GPU availability or a faster-whisper release changes the speed-path choice

nodes.definition: Decide the local model size and path: because overnight batch transcription has no latency constraint, even CPU-only whisper.cpp medium/large is sufficient for quality, and faster-whisper is used only if an NVIDIA GPU is present [ESTIMATE - design, MED-HIGH]. The controlling logic is that with no real-time deadline, accuracy (larger model) beats speed, and the memory table shows large fits under 4 GB RAM on CPU, so the default is the largest model the target machine's RAM allows, on CPU, escalating to faster-whisper's GPU path only when a GPU exists and the backlog is large. Smaller models are reserved for phone-class devices.

included: the no-latency-so-favour-accuracy rule
default = largest model the RAM allows on CPU
escalate to faster-whisper GPU only with an NVIDIA GPU and a large backlog
excluded: the underlying footprint table and speed claim (their own nodes)

pros.claim: Sizing for accuracy because batch has no deadline gets the best transcript quality on modest hardware
pros.example: defaulting to whisper.cpp large on CPU overnight rather than a fast-but-worse small model

cons.claim: The largest model can run long on a weak CPU, delaying the nightly grade write-back
cons.example: a large model on a low-end laptop not finishing the backlog before morning

failure_modes: choosing a small fast model when batch had no latency pressure and accuracy was free to buy
defaulting to the GPU path on a machine that has no GPU
acceptance_tests: the decision states that batch has no latency constraint, defaults to the largest CPU model the RAM allows, and escalates to faster-whisper GPU only when an NVIDIA GPU is present
revisit_triggers: the nightly run stops finishing before morning
hardware (RAM or GPU) changes
a smaller model proves accurate enough to save time

base.update_signal: a nightly-run overrun or a hardware change revises the model sizing

nodes.definition: Hold the binding privacy constraint: per the EDPB's Guidelines 02/2021 on Virtual Voice Assistants, voice recordings are personal data and become Article 9 'special category' biometric data when processed to uniquely identify a person (speaker-ID, voice embeddings, identity diarization); plain transcription without an identification purpose does not by itself trigger Article 9 [FACT via search snippets attributed to EDPB]. The design consequence is absolute: never run speaker identification on the recordings — the single-user system has no need to identify who is speaking, since it is always the one known learner. Transcription for grading is the permitted purpose; identity biometrics are out of scope by design.

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: the voice-capture pipeline is a go when every binding gate clears. edge_cases.mitigation: mark it failed(reason) with the reason stored, retry next night, and surface a persistent failure for inspection rather than dropping it

edge_cases.description: A mis-transcribed key term causes the LLM grader to mark a correct spoken answer wrong
edge_cases.trigger: the transcript garbles a load-bearing term the rubric checks
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the audio+transcript+grade audit link so the learner can dispute and the mis-transcription can be seen, and caveat grades on low-confidence transcripts

edge_cases.description: An LLM-structured voice note hallucinates a detail and would enter the KB unreviewed
edge_cases.trigger: the note post-processor over-structures a rambling recording and no human confirms it
edge_cases.mitigation: require human confirmation before any note/flashcard candidate enters the KB and show the note beside its linked audio moment

edge_cases.description: The nightly batch does not finish transcribing the backlog before morning on a weak CPU
edge_cases.trigger: a large day's answers run on whisper.cpp large on a low-end CPU with no GPU
edge_cases.mitigation: step down to a smaller model or, if an NVIDIA GPU is present, switch to faster-whisper's GPU path to clear the backlog

edge_cases.description: Whisper's language ID misdetects a short or code-mixed answer as the wrong language
edge_cases.trigger: a two-word or code-switched answer is fed to LID
edge_cases.mitigation: store the LID confidence, flag low-confidence detections, and let the grader treat a wrong-language transcript as unreliable rather than authoritative

edge_cases.description: Retained answer audio accumulates indefinitely, widening the personal-data surface even with no speaker-ID
edge_cases.trigger: the audit link keeps every recording forever with no retention policy
edge_cases.mitigation: prune audio under a retention policy once the item is no longer pedagogically live, keeping the transcript and grade for the record

edge_cases.description: An engine-specific cloud feature is wired directly into the worker, breaking the config-flag abstraction
edge_cases.trigger: a cloud-only capability is called outside the TranscriberInterface
edge_cases.mitigation: keep all engine calls behind the interface and drop or adapt engine-specific extras rather than leaking them into the worker

workflow.action: Record the owner's deferred-choice and any-language requirements
workflow.description: State the speak-any-language, save-and-queue brief and mark the local-vs-cloud engine as owner-deferred
workflow.gate: the deferral and the any-language requirement are stated with the one-interface consequence

workflow.action: Derive the async batch posture and capture spec
workflow.description: Derive the nightly async pipeline and the per-answer 16 kHz mono capture that only records and hands off
workflow.gate: the async-batch derivation and the per-answer capture format are stated

workflow.description: Write the metadata row with status=queued over a dir-of-files + SQLite store
workflow.gate: the metadata row and status=queued queue are defined with language_hint optional

workflow.description: Specify one interface with LocalWhisper and CloudSTT implementations and a uniform return
workflow.gate: the interface names both implementations and the config-flag-not-rewrite guarantee

workflow.action: Assess the local Whisper-class engine coverage and footprint
workflow.description: State the fetched 100-language count, the whisper.cpp memory table and the faster-whisper speed path
workflow.gate: the 100-language count, the memory table and the speed/accuracy trade are stated with honesty tags

workflow.action: Size the local model against hardware
workflow.description: Default to the largest CPU model the RAM allows because batch has no latency, escalating to GPU only with an NVIDIA GPU
workflow.gate: the no-latency-favour-accuracy rule and the GPU-escalation condition are stated

workflow.action: Catalogue the cloud STT options honestly
workflow.description: List Google 125+, Azure/Amazon UNKNOWN counts, OpenAI whisper-1 25 MB + ~57 languages, and Deepgram/AssemblyAI
workflow.gate: each vendor's coverage is stated with FACT/UNKNOWN tags and no invented numbers

workflow.action: Handle any language via language identification
workflow.description: Use Whisper LID with no picker, store detected language + confidence, flag low-confidence transcripts
workflow.gate: LID detects language with no picker, stores confidence, and flags unreliable transcripts

workflow.action: Run the nightly transcription worker with failure states
workflow.description: Drain status=queued through the interface nightly and govern items with the queued/transcribed/graded/failed state machine
workflow.gate: the worker is engine-agnostic and the no-silent-drop state machine is defined

workflow.action: Grade the transcript content and write back
workflow.description: Grade transcript content against the rubric, set the content-vs-delivery boundary, and write the grade to the mastery map with an audit link
workflow.gate: content is graded from the transcript, delivery is reserved for TOEFL-speaking, and the write-back keeps the audio+transcript+grade audit link

workflow.action: Structure voice notes with a human-confirm gate
workflow.description: Reuse record->transcribe, LLM-structure into note/flashcard candidates linked to audio, and require human confirmation
workflow.gate: notes are LLM-structured candidates, audio-linked, and blocked from the KB without human confirmation

workflow.action: Hold the privacy posture and compose the go/no-go
workflow.description: Never run speaker-ID, default to local, gate cloud behind consent + retention terms, and compose the merged verdict conditioning each go on its binding gate
workflow.gate: speaker-ID is off, cloud is gated behind consent + verified retention terms, and the verdict conditions every go on its binding gate

dominance_rules.rule: The never-run-speaker-ID rule dominates any voice-processing convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: speaker-ID / voice embeddings cross into Article 9 special-category biometric processing with no product need in a single-user system
dominance_rules.trigger: a feature would identify or distinguish speakers by voice
dominance_rules.action: refuse speaker-ID and satisfy the need with non-biometric means; keep processing to plain transcription

dominance_rules.rule: The consent-and-retention gate dominates any cloud coverage or accuracy edge
dominance_rules.rationale: cloud egress sends personal voice data off-machine and some vendors' terms are UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.trigger: cloud STT is proposed or its config flag is flipped
dominance_rules.action: keep audio local by default and enable cloud only with an explicit consent note and the vendor's verified current retention terms

dominance_rules.rule: The verified-count honesty dominates any convenient language number
dominance_rules.rationale: Azure and Amazon current language counts were not fetchable and must not be invented
dominance_rules.trigger: a cloud vendor's language count is stated
dominance_rules.action: quote only Google 125+ (vendor claim) and OpenAI ~57, and mark Azure/Amazon counts UNKNOWN until the live table is verified

dominance_rules.rule: Grade content from the transcript dominates grading delivery by default
dominance_rules.rationale: delivery lives in the audio and penalizing accent on a content course is wrong; SpeechRater-style delivery scoring is a TOEFL-speaking exception
dominance_rules.trigger: a grade would weigh pronunciation or fluency
dominance_rules.action: grade content only, reserve delivery scoring for an explicit TOEFL-speaking course, and keep the audio linked for that future step

dominance_rules.rule: The no-silent-drop state machine dominates best-effort processing
dominance_rules.rationale: a learner's spoken answer must never vanish without trace
dominance_rules.trigger: an item fails to transcribe or grade
dominance_rules.action: mark it failed(reason), store the reason, retry next night, and surface persistent failures instead of dropping them

dominance_rules.rule: The human-confirm gate dominates auto-ingesting voice notes
dominance_rules.rationale: an LLM-structured note can hallucinate and must not silently enter the KB
dominance_rules.trigger: a note/flashcard candidate is produced from a voice note
dominance_rules.action: require human confirmation beside the linked audio before the note enters the KB

dominance_rules.rule: Batch accuracy dominates transcription speed unless the nightly run overruns
dominance_rules.rationale: the overnight batch has no latency constraint, so a larger, more accurate model is the default
dominance_rules.action: default to the largest CPU model the RAM allows and only step down or move to a GPU path if the nightly run does not finish

dominance_rules.rule: The uniform interface dominates engine-specific features in the worker
dominance_rules.rationale: leaking engine-specific calls breaks the config-flag deferral the owner requires
dominance_rules.trigger: an engine-specific capability is wired into the worker
dominance_rules.action: keep all engine calls behind the TranscriberInterface and drop or adapt engine-specific extras

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the STT engine behind the TranscriberInterface from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a hard-coded engine forcing a rewrite when the owner resolves the deferred local-vs-cloud choice

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture per-answer 16 kHz mono files and enqueue a durable status row before transcription
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphaned recordings and a one-long-file capture that cannot retry a single answer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide never-run-speaker-ID and default-local before wiring any transcription
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to unwind Article 9 biometric processing or cloud egress added for convenience

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record consent and the vendor's current retention terms before enabling any cloud path
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping personal voice data to a vendor whose terms turn out to be unacceptable and must be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every cloud language count FACT or UNKNOWN when the catalogue is first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented Azure/Amazon count propagating into a decision and being retracted later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the content-not-delivery grading boundary and keep the audio linked from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding audio and foreclosing a TOEFL-speaking delivery step, or re-grading answers penalized for accent

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the queued/transcribed/graded/failed state machine with stored reasons before launch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silently dropped answers surfacing as lost learner data after the pipeline is live

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the audio+transcript+grade audit link when writing grades back
anti_rework_rules.prevents: un-disputable wrong marks that cannot be traced after the fact

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner resolves the local-vs-cloud engine decision
iteration_protocol.action: pin the configured implementation behind the interface, and if cloud, complete the consent-and-retention gate and re-run the go/no-go

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vendor's live language table or retention page becomes fetchable and resolves an UNKNOWN
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN count/term with the verified value and re-check the local-vs-cloud frame

iteration_protocol.trigger: a target language transcribes with unacceptable WER or the LID misdetects it repeatedly
iteration_protocol.action: flag the language, revisit the coverage-first assumption, and consider a cloud engine for that language behind the consent gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: the nightly batch stops finishing before morning
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the local model or, if an NVIDIA GPU is present, move to faster-whisper's GPU path

iteration_protocol.trigger: a TOEFL-speaking-style course is added that needs delivery scoring
iteration_protocol.action: add a delivery-scoring step reading the retained audio and revisit the content-vs-delivery boundary

iteration_protocol.trigger: updated EDPB/GDPR guidance changes the biometric or retention threshold
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the never-run-speaker-ID posture and the cloud consent-and-retention gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a mis-transcription is traced to a wrong grade or a retention limit forces pruning
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the low-confidence caveat and add a retention policy over the audit trail

priority_rationale: The owner's deferred-choice and any-language requirements come first because every capture, engine and privacy decision depends on them; the async posture, capture spec and store/enqueue model next, because they are the pipeline the transcription runs inside; the TranscriberInterface then operationalizes the deferral, and the local engine (coverage, footprint, speed, sizing), the cloud catalogue and language ID characterize the engine choices; the nightly worker, grading, precedent, content-vs-delivery boundary, write-back, failure states and note pipeline then turn a transcript into a graded, audited learner signal; and the privacy constraint, cloud consent gate, local-vs-cloud frame and the merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a privacy-safe, no-drop, defensible ship decision.
